subject: Preflight: ISO/FedRAMP audit boundary & evidence asks
messages:
From: Jane Cole <jane.cole@auditoria.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security <security@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Auditoria preflight: boundary confirmations and evidence window

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for agreeing to run a short preflight ahead of the formal intake. To help our intake team scope the ISO 27001 / FedRAMP assessment and map SIG/CAIQ items to controls, can you confirm the following?

1) Certification targets: are you planning ISO 27001 certification only, FedRAMP Moderate, or FedRAMP Moderate + ISO? We need to understand expected scope for artifact sampling.

2) Logical boundary: which service names and production clusters are in-scope? Please list service IDs or the short service names (not environment names).

3) Evidence window: preferred sampling window (last 12 months vs. last 6 months) and earliest available snapshots for configs and logs.

4) Key control owners: who owns access management, network controls, and encryption at-rest/email SRM? Names + emails suffice.

5) Delivery preference: will you provide artifacts via a shared Drive folder, S3 presigned links, or a dedicated secure upload endpoint? We ask because large log exports often need temporary credentials.

I attached our standardized preflight checklist for reference. If you can return answers inline below and a tentative timeline for the intake call, we can book next steps.

Cheers,

Jane Cole
Senior Engagement Manager
Auditoria Inc.
[Attachment: auditoria_preflight_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jane Cole <jane.cole@auditoria.com>
Cc: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Acme Security <security@acme-payments.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Auditoria preflight: boundary confirmations and evidence window

On Thu, Sep 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM Jane Cole <jane.cole@auditoria.com> wrote:
> Thanks for agreeing to run a short preflight ahead of the formal intake. To help our intake team scope the ISO 27001 / FedRAMP assessment and map SIG/CAIQ items to controls, can you confirm the following?
>
> 1) Certification targets...

Hi Jane — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers below and then a few follow-ups.

1) Certification targets:
- Primary target: ISO 27001 certification (company-wide) with an optional FedRAMP Moderate readiness track for our API-hosted inference product (redwood-api). We expect to decide on the formal FedRAMP path after the initial ISO cert.

2) Logical boundary:
- In-scope: redwood-api (production clusters: rw-prod-01, rw-prod-02), serving runtime (inference-engine) and control plane services that process customer requests. Excluded: internal analytics sandbox and experimental model-training infra.

3) Evidence window:
- Prefer last 12 months for sampling. Most logs retained for 13 months; config snapshots available back to 14 months for primary clusters.

4) Key control owners:
- Access & IdM: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
- Network/security infra: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
- Encryption & keys: Rachel Kim (me) — I own the KMS policy coordination with customers.

5) Delivery preference:
- Prefer shared Drive for configs and small artifacts. For large log exports we will provide S3 presigned links scoped to the auditor IP ranges for a 72-hour window.

Follow-ups / asks:
- Can you confirm whether FedRAMP evidence expectations differ for readiness versus full authorization (just a high-level list)?
- Do you require unredacted logs for sampling, or is hashed/trimmed data acceptable (we have customer PII masks in many logs)?
- We will upload a draft audit_scope_matrix.xlsx to the drive by EOD; would you prefer we include a column mapping each artifact to SIG/CAIQ questions or keep that separate?

I'll attach the scope matrix after I sync with Markus/OlgA. Agree to schedule a 30-minute preflight call early next week — proposed slots below.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tentative_slots.txt (plain text)]

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jane Cole <jane.cole@auditoria.com>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Acme Security <security@acme-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Auditoria preflight: boundary confirmations and evidence window

Hi Jane and team — adding technical detail and artifact ownership to accelerate intake.

- Evidence indexing: we will provide an "evidence_index_sample.pdf" with a few exemplar artifacts mapped to control IDs (attached). That file shows format; if that's acceptable we'll expand to full index.

- Logs and retention:
  * API access logs: stored in rw-logs-prod S3 (13 months retention). We can export session slices (JSON) and redact IPs on demand.
  * Keystore/KMS audit trails: Cloud KMS audit entries retained in audit-project-logs for 2 years.
  * Network flow logs: VPC Flow logs stored centrally (30 days in hot store, archived to cold for 12 months).

- Sampling approach suggestion: provide 3 sample days across the 12-month window (one recent, one mid-window, one older). For high-volume logs we will provide pre-filtered extracts keyed by request-id to limit PII exposure.

- S3 access: we will create auditor-focused IAM roles and presigned links limited to the auditor IP ranges. Please confirm your static IPs or a CIDR block we can trust.

- Diagrams: we will include a current data flow diagram and a boundary diagram (SVG + PDF). We anticipate uploading the audit_scope_matrix.xlsx + evidence_index_sample.pdf by EOD Sep 4.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evidence_index_sample.pdf (pdf), data_flow_diagram.svg (image)]

From: Jane Cole <jane.cole@auditoria.com>

Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Auditoria preflight: boundary confirmations and evidence window

Thanks Rachel/Olga — this is exactly what we need to scope intake. A few quick confirmations and next steps: 

- FedRAMP: readiness artifacts differ from full authorization primarily in continuous monitoring expectations and FedRAMP-specific POA&Ms. For a readiness engagement we'll limit sampling to configuration & process evidence and perform a mapping exercise; full authorization will require runtime evidence and continuous monitoring pipelines. We'll detail this in the intake call.

- Logs: hashed/trimmed logs are acceptable for initial sampling; if we need to validate a detection/incident we will request unredacted slices under a narrow NDA clause.

- IPs: our auditor network appears on the CIDR list 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24 — you can provision presigned links for those ranges and we will acknowledge once we've tested access.

Next steps:
1) We'll take the evidence_index_sample.pdf and confirm format.
2) Book a 30-minute intake call: proposed times Tue Sep 7 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed Sep 8 14:00-14:30 PT. Please confirm a slot and we will send a calendar invite.

Appreciate the prompt turnaround — looking forward to the drive link and the scope matrix.

Regards,
Jane Cole
Senior Engagement Manager
Auditoria Inc.
